title: Paraguay's President Removed From Office After Bank Collapse
summary: Paraguay's president has been removed from office after a bank collapse left millions unable to reach their money. President Santiago Peña was impeached on Friday, just days after Ueno Bank, a digital bank, collapsed earlier in the week. The collapse left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts. About three million depositors still cannot reach their savings and pensions. The bank was seized by Paraguay's central bank, and people in the capital, Asunción, have protested. Lawmakers voted to remove Peña. The Senate voted 44 to 0, with one lawmaker absent. The charges included conflicts of interest, interference with regulators, and diverted pension funds. Peña held shares until last year in the company that owned the bank, but he has denied any wrongdoing. Senate president Basilio Núñez said Pena was found guilty of failing in his duties. Peña was arrested on Friday and placed under house arrest. His deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as interim president and will serve until 2028. Alliana promised that people affected by the collapse will be fully compensated.
why_it_matters: It matters because families keep their savings in banks, and when a bank fails, a family may not be able to pay for the things it needs.

background_read: A bank is a place where people keep their money safe, and a digital bank lets people use their money through a phone or computer instead of going to a building.
When a bank collapses, people can suddenly lose access to their savings, and the country's central bank may step in to take control of it.
A president is the leader of a country, and lawmakers can vote to remove a president from the job if they believe the leader failed in their duties.
